decision.title: libmpdec keeps no large buffers on the stack

body.p: , amending . Upstream transpose.c holds two SIDE*SIDE-word buffers in squaretrans_pow2 (128 KiB with 32-bit words) and two BUFSIZE-word buffers in swap_halfrows_pow2 (32 KiB). Every product of more than 1024 words (on WebAssembly 9216 digits, smaller operand above 2304) whose transform is not a power of two up to 4096 words takes the four- or six-step path through them and trapped on the 64 KiB WebAssembly stack; an untrusted query could do it within the default digit limit.

item.p: Patch ("sxml patch ()" in transpose.c): both pairs are one heap block from mpd_alloc (the current decimal scope, ), sized for the actual block; squaretrans_pow2 now returns 0 on failure and transpose_pow2 passes it on, so the product reports MPD_Malloc_error (OUT_OF_MEMORY) and leaks nothing.

Audit (-fstack-usage, wasm32 at -Os): after the patch the largest libmpdec frame is 1248 bytes (mpd_qpowmod; 2.5 KiB on x86-64 GCC); the MPD_MINALLOC_MAX (64-word) buffers in mpdecimal.c, basearith.c and io.c and the 3-word arrays in fourstep.c, sixstep.c, crt.c, numbertheory.c stay. Measured by painting the stack under wasm: multiply needs 785 bytes, divide and integer divide at most 2.9 KiB, flat from 5000 to 16,000,000 digits.

Recursion ( exempts libmpdec): only _kmul_worksize, _karatsuba_rec (operands of at most 1024 words: depth 7) and _karatsuba_rec_fnt recurse. The last runs only for products above 3 * 2^25 words on 32-bit targets, more than two MPD_MAX_PREC (425 million digit) operands have, and above 3 * 2^32 words on 64-bit ones, depth log2 of the size ratio with frames under 100 bytes. Newton division and the integer power sxml uses are loops. So no recursion patch and no lower cap on maximum_digit_count are needed.

Tests (tests/decimal_test.c): squares and quotients at 10,000 digits (four-step on wasm), 10^6000 * 10^6000 and two 10,000-digit operands refused with LIMIT_EXCEEDED, 60,000 digits (the plain six-step path on wasm), and every allocation failure of a long product reported and clean.
